sources.ecoli_source: Passerat et al. 2011, Water Research 45:893 (Seine CSO): 'The CSO contained 1.5 x 10^6 E. coli per 100 mL on average'; range 4.6-7.3 log10 (Wang et al. 2026). https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/20934197/
sources.ammonia_source: Derived: crude sewage ~39 mg N/L (GOV.UK, septic tank and package treatment plants: typical concentrations) diluted ~10x by runoff in storm overflows (Passerat et al. 2011: 89% of CSO discharge was surface runoff). No measured UK value found.
sources.ecoli_k: Servais et al. 2007, HESS 11:1581: 45e-3 per hour at 20 C, temperature dependent; Seine 0.19-0.81 per day. Winter 0.5, summer 1.1 per day. https://hess.copernicus.org/articles/11/1581/2007/
sources.ammonia_k: Judgement within Pauer & Auer 2009 (nitrification velocity 0.14-0.97 m/day, i.e. ~0.1-1 per day for 1 m depth). https://digitalcommons.mtu.edu/michigantech-p/6309
sources.ammonia_bg: Bowes et al. 2018, ESSD 10:1637, Table 3: Cherwell 0.031, Thames at Swinford 0.039 mg N/L. https://essd.copernicus.org/articles/10/1637/2018/
sources.ecoli_bg: Order of magnitude only: Servais et al. 2007 (100-1000 per 100 mL in small streams); EA samples at Wolvercote Mill Stream reported 300 in June 2022 (news report). No proper median found.
sources.swim: Bathing Water Regulations 2013 Schedule 5 (inland, E. coli per 100 mL): Excellent 500, Good 1000 (95th percentile). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2013/1675/schedule/5/made
sources.fish: WFD (Standards and Classification) Directions (England and Wales) 2015, Sch 3 Table 7, lowland high alkalinity: total ammonia Good 0.6, Moderate 1.1 mg N/L (90th percentile). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2015/1623
sources.velocity: EA time-of-travel database (Guymer, Warwick): most traces 0.05-0.5 m/s, rising with discharge; spills happen at high flow. https://www2.warwick.ac.uk/fac/sci/eng/research/grouplist/water/events/britcouncildyetracing/2_mixing_in_rivers.pdf
